listing.blurb: A long-running exhibition at Whitechapel Gallery, the public gallery on Whitechapel High Street, devoted to Cecilia Vicuña. It stays up until mid-February 2027, so it's easy to fit in.

story.who: Cecilia Vicuña is an artist, poet and activist, and the gallery's own website counts her among the best-known artists from Latin America. Her work crosses painting, textile, photography, installation and film. She has made quipus for over fifty years, and she studied at the Slade School of Art in London in the early 1970s, with a studio in Stepney Green.
story.then: According to the gallery's own website, Vicuña left Chile after the 1973 coup. This installation concludes the wider exhibition. In 1974 she co-founded an organisation in London to stand with Chile and other liberation struggles.
story.now: Foraging Quipu is the closing work of the wider exhibition. It was first made at the Irish Museum of Modern Art in Dublin in 2025. For London, local people were invited to gather dry plant matter and light debris from their surroundings, and these contributions are woven into a hanging quipu, modelled on the Andean knotted cords once used to keep records. Branches, seeds, roots, fungi, textiles and plastics all sit together in it, according to the gallery.
worth_knowing: The gallery's website calls the exhibition this belongs to the first major UK exhibition of Vicuña's work.
It is shown as part of a wider exhibition, which opens with her Quipu Menstrual.
